strengths: Clear and well-motivated framework using draft model lookahead for improved token importance estimation
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (RULER, LongBench, MileBench) with consistent improvements up to 25 points
First application of draft lookahead to KV cache optimization (SpecKV); extends SpecPrefill framework to multiple inference optimizations
Theoretical justification via multiple theorems with empirical validation of attention correlation (R²=0.99 for mean aggregation)
Broad applicability demonstrated across model families, scales, and multimodal models with practical compatibility
Thorough ablation studies and reproducibility documentation with code promised
weaknesses: Incremental novelty over SpecPrefill [36]; conceptual advancement is modest—primarily extends existing draft-based approach to KV dropping

Heavy dependence on draft model quality (Fig. 11) with no principled guidance for draft selection; requires additional memory overhead
Substantial hyperparameter sensitivity (n_lookahead, n_window, l_skip, etc.) with task-dependent performance and no systematic tuning methodology
Insufficient analysis of failure modes: weak attention correlations (Gemma R²=0.33) and unexplained performance improvements in some cases deserve deeper investigation

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across RULER, LongBench, and MileBench with multiple model families and extensive ablation studies
Consistent performance improvements over strong baselines (SnapKV, LAQ++) with practical efficiency gains (40-75% latency reduction at 64k context)
Theoretical contributions providing mathematical justification via Theorems 1-3 connecting output approximation to attention approximation error
Well-motivated framework unifying and extending lookahead-based approximate inference techniques
Thorough implementation details and reproducibility commitment with code release promise
Practical cascaded SpecKV-PC approach achieving substantial memory savings (~25GB at 64k)
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: primarily combines existing lookahead ideas from LAQ++ and SpecPrefill rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Theoretical limitations: Theorem 1 assumes unrealistic 1-1 token correspondence; Theorem 2 requires RIP which transformers likely don't satisfy; bounds are loose with problem-dependent constants
Unfair experimental comparison: SpecKV uses nlookahead=full-output while LAQ++ uses fixed nlookahead=8, making direct comparison inequitable
Modest empirical improvements: often 1-3 percentage points over LAQ++ (e.g., 48.80 vs 48.43 in Table 2), questioning practical significance
High method complexity with multiple hyperparameters (nwindow, k, nslash, nvert, lskip) lacking principled justification and showing task-dependent sensitivity
Critical draft model dependency with significant cross-family degradation (5-10 point drops in Table 7), limiting generalizability and applicability in constrained settings

Counter-intuitive findings under-explored: SpecPC shows minimal improvement with longer lookahead (Fig. 19); sparser prefill sometimes helps unexpectedly (Fig. 20b), suggesting incomplete theoretical understanding
Cascaded SpecKV-PC requires aggressive compression (2048 tokens) for benefits and brittle to extreme compression (>5 point drops), limiting robustness

strengths: Important problem: Addresses real bottlenecks in long-context LLM inference (quadratic attention, linear KV cache memory)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple benchmarks (RULER, LongBench, MileBench), model families (Qwen, Llama), with consistent improvements over strong baselines
Strong practical impact: SpecKV-PC achieves 40-75% speedup with 25GB memory savings at 64K context vs LAQ++
Thorough ablation studies: Examines draft quality, lookahead length, sparse prefilling sparsity, cross-family robustness
Solid theoretical grounding: Theorems 1-3 provide bounds on importance error; Figure 2 empirically validates theory-practice connection
Clear presentation: Well-motivated, clear algorithmic descriptions, effective visualizations, comprehensive complexity comparison (Table 1)
Reproducibility commitment: Detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, extensive appendices, promised code release
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: Theorem 1 is straightforward spectral analysis; Theorem 2 relies on strong unverified RIP assumption for embeddings; Theorem 3 bound is loose (exponential terms)
Theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 assumes strict token alignment, but Eq. 2 uses ad-hoc centroid distance relaxation without theoretical justification
Incremental over prior work: SpecKV vs LAQ++ mainly differs in draft model choice (not conceptually novel); SpecPC extends SpecPrefill with modest gains; SpecKV-PC is straightforward combination
Dependence on draft model: Requires reasonably accurate draft model; cross-family SpecPC shows 4-5 point degradation; no principled guidance for draft selection
Experimental sample sizes: Only 5 samples per RULER task, 50 from LongBench for main results; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
LAQ++ comparison: Uses authors' own implementation rather than official code, raising fairness concerns
Incomplete failure analysis: No exploration of when lookahead hurts or task-specific failure modes despite rare negative results
Missing assumptions verification: RIP assumption for Theorem 2 is unverified for actual LLM embeddings; Theorem 1 assumes ‖x_j‖₂ ≤ √d without validation
